paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: trusting the LORD isn't just a feeling, it shows up in what you tear down. Hezekiah "trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel," and then he went and removed the things that were pulling people away from Him (2 Kings 18:4-5). Even the bronze snake Moses made had to go, because Israel had been burning incense to it (2 Kings 18:4; Numbers 21:9). A good thing can turn into a wrong thing when it takes the place that belongs to God, and I'd rather find that out in my own kitchen than later.

Now look at what trusting got him. Hezekiah "remained faithful to the LORD and did not turn from following Him," and "the LORD was with Hezekiah, and he prospered wherever he went" (2 Kings 18:6-7). He didn't follow God for a season and then drift off. That's the kind of steady I want, the kind that keeps showing up long after the first batch is cooling.

Then the passage puts Israel right beside him, and the difference is hard to miss. Samaria fell because the Israelites "did not listen to the voice of the LORD their God," and they "would neither listen nor obey" (2 Kings 18:12). Listening to God and obeying Him is the road that keeps us close to Him, and tuning Him out is the road that leads away. So, baker, ask yourself what you might need to set down so that your trust stays on the LORD alone. And keep that oven warm, because this story is NOT over.
